summary: Russia is permissive for the roof rat. Federal Law 498-FZ ('On Responsible Treatment of Animals') lets the government publish a list of species banned from private keeping — and neither the old Decree 795/2019 nor its replacement (Disposition 1163-r, in force 1 Sept 2025) lists ANY Rattus among the ~121 prohibited taxa (those are big carnivores, primates, elephants, cetaceans, etc.). The ordinary decorative/fancy rat (R. norvegicus domestica) is kept and sold freely with no permit, and because R. rattus is nowhere prohibited, the same route applies to captive-bred roof rats. R. rattus does sit on a scientific invasive-species advisory list (SEVIN Top-100) but that carries NO enforceable keeping ban. Selling/giving needs only the normal vet documentation (vet passport / accompanying certificate); internal transport uses a vet Form 1 (between regions) or Form 4 (local), and import from outside the EAEU uses the EAEU veterinary-certificate regime via Rosselkhoznadzor.

keep.why: R. rattus is not named in the Art. 10 / 498-FZ prohibited-keeping list (Disposition 1163-r, 2025, nor the prior Decree 795/2019), so no exotic permit applies; it's kept under the same regime as the decorative R. norvegicus (Art. 13 welfare duties only). The SEVIN Top-100 invasive listing is advisory, not a legal bar. (A one-line Rosselkhoznadzor confirmation that R. rattus is treated as a 'decorative animal' would remove all doubt.)
keep.governing_law: Federal Law 498-FZ Art. 10, 13; Disposition 1163-r (08.05.2025) — Rattus not listed.

breed.why: No licence/registration for private non-commercial breeding of decorative rodents (498-FZ Arts. 8–9 define 'nurseries/kennels' with welfare/vet-supervision duties, not a state licence for hobby breeding). Commercial-scale breeding triggers vet oversight under the Law on Veterinary Medicine (No. 4979-1). R. rattus not prohibited; in practice Russian breeders treat it like R. norvegicus.
breed.governing_law: 498-FZ Arts. 8–9; Law on Veterinary Medicine No. 4979-1.

sell_give.why: Sale of decorative rodents is allowed but must follow the Retail Trade Rules (Decree 2463/2020, Section IX): the seller provides a vet passport/accompanying document, species/care info, and confirmation the species isn't on the prohibited list. No seller's licence for private transactions; free giving is unregulated beyond welfare. R. rattus may be sold/given exactly as R. norvegicus.

transport.why: Internal transport needs a state-vet accompanying document (Form 1 across regions; Form 4 local). International import (from a non-EAEU country) uses the EAEU Unified Veterinary Certificate Form 41 (CTS Decision 607/2011) with a ~21-day pre-export quarantine + origin health certificate, presented to the Rosselkhoznadzor border post (VetIS/Mercury e-cert); a simplified travellers' regime (CTS Decision 317/2010 Ch. 15) may apply to ≤2 non-commercial animals — confirm with Rosselkhoznadzor. Never release.
transport.governing_law: CTS Decision 607/2011 (Form 41); CTS Decision 317/2010 (Ch. 15/40); vet-transport rules; 498-FZ Art. 13.

restrictions.summary: Selling/transporting a decorative rat in Russia needs vet documentation (vet passport for sale; Form 1/Form 4 for movement; EAEU Form 41 + quarantine for third-country import). No keeping permit. Never release a roof rat.

inquiry_focus: (1) Does Rosselkhoznadzor classify captive-bred Rattus rattus (чёрная крыса) kept as a decorative pet the same as the decorative R. norvegicus (no permit), or as a 'wild animal' requiring authorization? (2) Which EAEU veterinary certificate is required to import 1–3 captive-bred decorative R. rattus from a third country — Form 41 (CTS 607/2011) or the simplified travellers' regime (CTS 317/2010 Ch. 15) — and is pre-import quarantine mandatory? (3) Is any registration/notification required to commercially breed and sell captive-bred R. rattus, and under which instrument?
